stories.title: Oddsmakers rank starting QBs by POINT-SPREAD VALUE: JA clear #1
stories.summary:
His point-spread value is 7.23, which is almost a full point ahead of the next QB!



	 



	



	 



	“‘To me, he's the most talented QB in the league,’ one oddsmaker told me. ‘The durability as well would put him ahead of Mahomes.’



	 



	To that point, Allen hasn't missed a game since his rookie season, and at 6-foot-5, 237 pounds he is able to punish defensive backs, safeties and even linebackers when he chooses to run the ball. Allen has at least 421 rushing yards in every season of his career and scored 14 rushing TDs (along with 3,668 yards and 25 TDs passing) this past season.



	
	As one oddsmaker put it: ‘He is the entire Bills identity right now.’



	 



	Not one, but two oddsmakers had Allen worth nine points more to the spread than his new backup Kyle Allen and Josh Allen was the only QB that all 11 oddsmakers had as worth at least worth six points against the number.”

An interesting thing to keep an eye on - Can Brady fix yearly mid season swoon?
stories.summary:
Something that was a constant issue under McD is the team's apparent loss of focus somewhere in the early middle of the schedule where they suddenly go from whomping teams to losing games they shouldn't and it ends up costing them the #1 seed at the end of the year.



	 



	It will be interesting to see if Brady is able to keep them mentally focused and not allow them to get overconfident and think they can just show up to games against some lesser teams and win during these stretches.



	 



	I know it's a long season but it gets kind of annoying seeing how good this team is over the course of the last 6-7 years, having the best record in the NFL during that time, an absurd point differential that is 200 points higher than the next closest team, but yet they can never get the #1 seed because this constantly is an issue every single year.



	 



	At some point you would think McD would have figured out how to get the players attention on this based on how things usually went but for whatever reason he never was.



	 



	Will Brady be able to? That's the thing I'm most interested in finding out this year.

stories.title: CJGJ = Problem Child?
stories.summary:
As many of you have, I have been tuned into the offseason/Training Camp and I have to be honest, I am seeing something brewing that makes me feel uneasy.  It's CJ Gardner-Johnson.  When they first signed him, I was like ok, they got a dawg style guy with some talent.  Hey we need some dawgs and this could help our defense.  However, after seeing the constant sh***t talking and now this whole streaming "thing" with Brady and then going live after to talk about it.  It's clear to me this guy just doesn't get it.  Almost like some Antonio Brown vibes.  He has had issues with his former teams.  Quite a few teams I might add. 



	 



	There was a certain culture developed here over the past 8-9 years. You heard Jim Leonhard reference it in his presser regarding the level of professionalism that is displayed by the players.  I fully understand if it gets out of control they can just cut him, but I hope this guy doesn't kill the vibes and make training camp unenjoyable for everyone. This can have a ripple effect throughout the team.  He appears to be the exact type of player (attitude and maturity) we have tried to avoid over the last 9 years.

stories.title: Dion Dawkins loses 45 pounds
stories.summary:
Interesting that he was previously upset with fans for criticizing his weight, but glad he decided to do something about it. His weight certainly looked like a problem the last several years as he was getting beat in key moments, and even looking like he was taking plays off.
	 



	
		Quote
	

	
		
			Buffalo Bills offensive tackle Dion Dawkins is going to have a new look ahead of the 2026 NFL season.
		

		
			 
		

		
			Dawkins told USA TODAY's Ralphie Aversa at the 2026 ESPYs he was feeling "good" ahead of the upcoming season. The 32-year-old tackle acknowledged that was because of a key change he made for the campaign.
		

		
			 
		

		
			"I've told [everyone] in the world that this will be the lightest season that I ever play," Dawkins said.
		

		
			Dawkins was listed as weighing 320 pounds by the Bills during the 2025 NFL season. The 6-5 tackle acknowledged he had dropped 45 pounds since his peak, though it wasn't clear whether his peak was his listed weight.
		

		
			 
		

		
			What was Dawkins' goal in dropping that weight?
		

		
			"To play a little faster, play a little better because something is not getting us over that hump," Dawkins said. "So I want to be at the best that I could possibly be. So I said, (expletive) it, let's lose some weight."
		

		
			 
		

		
			Dawkins noted he was still confident in his athleticism playing at a heavier weight. Still, he thought changing things up could benefit the Bills as they seek the right combination to get the team to the Super Bowl for the first time since 1994.
		

		
			 
		

		
			"I am fast heavy," Dawkins explained, "but I might be just a little bit faster, lighter. And that might be what Josh [Allen] needs to get us over that hump."
		

		
			Of course, Dawkins also detailed that Allen hadn't yet seen him at the lighter weight.
		

		
			 
		

		
			"He'll probably see me and be like, 'All right, Dion, it's time to eat a little bit,'" Dawkins said. "But I would rather have that than all right Dion's time to lose a little bit. So I'd rather start super light and see how it goes."
		

		
			 
		

		
			The good news for the veteran tackle? First-year Bills coach Joe Brady is on board with his plan to drop weight.
		

		
			"If I come in lighter, I get a couple of the touchdown passes," Dawkins joked when asked about Brady. "So we'll see."
		
	



	
	https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/bills-o-lineman-lost-45-003413717.html
